lots.what_it_is: Ten British coins in card flips, hand-graded in pen (not professionally graded): half crowns 1921, 1922, 1927, 1929 x2, 1946 x2, 1955 and florins 1922, 1929. Nine are .500 silver (all pre-1947 dates, including the two 1946 half crowns, which the researcher wrongly called cupro-nickel); only the 1955 half crown is cupro-nickel.
lots.guide_summary: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. No comparable could be opened (web search budget exhausted). Melt reference only, not a comp: 7 half crowns x 0.2273 oz + 2 florins x 0.1818 oz = about 1.95 oz fine silver; Kitco page opened 29 Sep 2026 shows silver US$60.65/oz and AUD 1.4335 per USD, so about A$86.9/oz and about A$170 melt. Bullion buyers typically pay under melt.
lots.working: No SOLD entries, so both maximums are 0 under the rules. For context only: melt about A$170; a hammer of $100 would be $122 all-in, well under melt, but this is not a SOLD-based bid limit.
lots.confidence_reason: Dates and denominations read clearly from the flips, but there is no SOLD evidence; value rests on a silver melt calculation.
lots.key_photo_findings: All ten flips legible. George V half crowns 1921, 1922, 1929 x2 and florins 1922, 1929 show the bust side; the 1927 half crown shows the shield reverse (enlarged crop too soft to confirm first or second reverse type; second type 1927 is proof only, so this is almost certainly the common circulation type). 1946 George VI half crowns pen-graded EF and UNC. 1955 Elizabeth II half crown shield side. Coins look evenly worn, no obvious holes or damage at this resolution.
lots.condition: Circulated, roughly VF to EF by eye; pen grades are the vendor's own and likely optimistic.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are all ten coins present as pictured, and are any cleaned or damaged? (The 1927 half crown: which reverse type?)

lots.key_photo_findings: Florin legend 'PARLIAMENT HOUSE AUSTRALIA ONE FLORIN 1927' clear, nicely toned, light wear. Medal enlarged reads 'NEW SOUTH WALES RAILWAYS' with arms, two locomotives and date 1955, so it is the 1955 centenary piece, not an 1855 medal; metal unknown. In the coin box, two white 50c coins look round at this angle; the right one shows arms with '50' at top, which could be a 1966 round 50c (80% silver) but may be 12-sided seen obliquely. Notes circulated.
lots.condition: Circulated throughout; florin about VF-EF by eye.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are either of the 50c coins the 1966 round (silver) type? What metal is the 1955 NSW Railways medal, and are all the notes shown included?
